# ui-memory

The memory page and quick capture: lasting memories seen, added, edited, forgotten, searched and consolidated.

- **Runs in:** the UI (your Emacs)
- **Source:** [lisp/ui/harness-ui-memory.el](../../lisp/ui/harness-ui-memory.el)
- **Loaded:** when enabled (see `harness-enable-modules`)
- **Requires:** [ui](ui.md)
- **Brings along:** [memory](memory.md) (the rest of it)

## About

The lasting memories (harness-memory.el) on a page of their own:
what the agent and the user saved, in the two scopes, grouped by kind,
with the buttons that add, edit, forget, search and consolidate them.
`C-c h M` opens it; `C-c h m` captures one from anywhere.

The page reads, top to bottom (the project is the buffer's, as the
settings page's is):

  Memory  harness                3 memories · 2 project memories · 1 user memory
  Add Search Consolidate Refresh

  Project · harness                              Add Consolidate
  Preference
    • Don't import inside function bodies: put imports at the top.
      Preference · Aug 12                        Edit Forget
  Fact
    • The deploy target is Fly.io.
      Fact · Aug 12                              Edit Forget

  User                                           Add Consolidate
    • Prefer short answers and no filler.
      Preference · Aug 12                        Edit Forget

Its states say "Loading memories…", "No memories", "No project
memories", "No user memories", "No matches for “QUERY”" or "Memory
unavailable"; a search in effect says "Matches for “QUERY”" with
[Clear].

A click or RET on a button does what its key does: a adds to the
project, A to the user's memories, e edits the memory at point, d
forgets it, / searches, c and C consolidate the project's memories and
the user's, g loads the page again, and C-u m captures a user memory
rather than the project's.  The page adds the memories the harness
announces (`memory/changed`), once for a burst of them, and asks again
when the UI connects to a harness again.

Nothing here reads the memories directly: the page is a client, and
asks `_harness/memory/list`, `search`, `add`, `update`, `delete` and
`consolidate`, so it works the same against a harness server
elsewhere.

## Provides

### Commands

- `harness-memories` — Show the lasting memories for DIRECTORY's project.
- `harness-remember` — Save TEXT as a lasting memory, and say so.
- `harness-ui-memories-add` — Add a memory to SCOPE, project or user.
- `harness-ui-memories-add-user` — Add a memory to the user's memories.
- `harness-ui-memories-clear` — Clear the search and list every memory again.
- `harness-ui-memories-consolidate` — Consolidate the memories of SCOPE with a cheap model.
- `harness-ui-memories-edit` — Edit memory ID.
- `harness-ui-memories-forget` — Forget memory ID, or the one at point.
- `harness-ui-memories-refresh` — Load the memory page again.
- `harness-ui-memories-search` — Search the memories for QUERY, or list them all when it is empty.

## Uses

### Methods it calls

- `memory/add` ([memory](memory.md))
- `memory/consolidate` ([memory](memory.md))
- `memory/delete` ([memory](memory.md))
- `memory/list` ([memory](memory.md))
- `memory/search` ([memory](memory.md))
- `memory/update` ([memory](memory.md))

### Events it hears over ACP

- `memory/changed` → `harness-ui-memories--on-event`

### Hooks it adds to

- `harness-ui-event-functions` → `harness-ui-memories--on-event`
- `harness-ui-redraw-hook` → `harness-ui-memories--redraw-all`
